title: Nurturing and Sustaining Long-Term Relationships
heading: Nurturing and Sustaining Long-Term Relationships

sourceRefs.role: chapter title and official positioning support

coreClaim: Long-term relationships last only when reciprocity, repair, and maintenance continue after the initial bond forms.
distinctMechanism: Durability depends on repeated upkeep rather than assuming closeness will sustain itself.
requiredAnchors: Reciprocity still matters after closeness forms.
Repair matters when distance or strain appears.
specificApplications: Sustain a friendship or work bond through repeated attention.
Notice one-sided maintenance before the relationship thins.
Address drift or strain before distance hardens.
commonMisreadings: Reciprocity matters only during early attraction.
Repair must be dramatic to count.
hardEdgeRequirement: Hard depth must preserve that even strong bonds can erode under neglect or one-sided effort.
thresholdQuestion: What keeps a close relationship durable instead of merely familiar?
